# Story 3.2: Enforce root-side mutation authority before create adjudication

Status: review

<!-- Note: Validation is optional. Run validate-create-story for quality check before dev-story. -->

## Story

As root orchestration,
I want to validate dialogue-side draft mutations against policy,
so that only legal proposals reach `createmachine`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a dialogue child proposal tries to mark a value `approved` or set `addressed=true`, when root evaluates the mutation, then root rejects it, restores the last legal draft, and emits structured feedback.
2. Given a dialogue child proposal is structurally legal, when root validates it, then root forwards it to `createmachine` for semantic adjudication.

## Sequencing / Dependencies

- Target confirmed: Epic 3, Story 3.2.
- Required predecessors: Epic 1 stories 1.1–1.3, Epic 2 stories 2.1–2.3, and Story 3.1, because root-side authority validation depends on durable workflow state, stable `flowId`, baseline/versioning, supervised dialogue routing, index context, and lookup brokerage.
- This story sets up Story 3.3, where the explicit create adjudication command path is completed on the create side.
- If repo behavior conflicts with older assumptions, prefer `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture.md`.

## Tasks / Subtasks

- [x] Add a shared root-side create-draft mutation policy surface (AC: 1, 2)
  - [x] Create a single shared policy module for dialogue-side create-draft mutation rules instead of scattering checks across root and create.
  - [x] Encode root-owned authority rules that reject dialogue proposals which change `createPlan`, introduce `approved`, set `addressed=true`, target the wrong `flowId`, use a stale base revision, or structurally violate the plan-shaped draft surface.
  - [x] Keep this policy focused on authority legality only; do not move semantic validation into root.

- [x] Validate dialogue proposals in root against the persisted legal baseline before forwarding (AC: 1, 2)
  - [x] Compare inbound proposal payloads against the persisted authoritative state from the workflow record / response baseline.
  - [x] Reject stale proposals before any deeper mutation diffing or downstream forwarding occurs.
  - [x] Only if the proposal is structurally legal and current should root forward it into the create adjudication path.

- [x] Restore last legal state and emit structured feedback on rejection (AC: 1)
  - [x] When root rejects an illegal proposal, restore the last legal authoritative draft bundle rather than leaving partially mutated state in flight.
  - [x] Emit machine-usable structured feedback describing why the proposal was rejected.
  - [x] Keep the flow alive after rejection so dialogue can continue from corrected authoritative state.

- [x] Prepare the root → create handoff seam without relocating semantic adjudication (AC: 2)
  - [x] Forward structurally legal proposals through the create adjudication seam expected by Story 3.3.
  - [x] Do not implement semantic approval logic, reopening rules, or persistence authority in root.
  - [x] Keep `createmachine` as the sole authority for approval semantics and persistence once a proposal passes root policy checks.

- [x] Keep Story 3.2 tightly scoped to root-side authority checks only (AC: 1, 2)
  - [x] Do not implement the full create-side adjudication command handling here; that belongs to Story 3.3.
  - [x] Do not redesign response supervision, lookup brokerage, or flow-first ingress.
  - [x] Do not add UI/session rendering work.

- [x] Address Senior Developer QA Findings (AC: 1)
  - [x] Emit structured stale-proposal feedback from `src/stately-studio/actors/workflow-reducer.ts` when `isStaleCreateDialogueProposal(...)` is true.
  - [x] Reject duplicate field, stat block, and relation entries in `src/stately-studio/actors/shared/create-draft-mutation-policy.ts` instead of allowing `Map` normalization to overwrite malformed proposals.
  - [x] Require every planned progression column to be present in each proposed progression level before root authority approval.

- [x] Address BMAD review findings from the latest QA pass (AC: 1, 2)
  - [x] Reject nested stat-block entries with duplicate `fieldKey` values before Map normalization can overwrite malformed proposals.
  - [x] Treat sparse or null progression levels as invalid proposals instead of silently continuing past them.
  - [x] Guard progression-level `values` before column-presence validation so malformed entries return structured feedback instead of throwing.

## Latest Review Findings



## Prior Review Findings

- Resolved — `src/stately-studio/actors/shared/create-draft-mutation-policy.ts`
  - Duplicate `fieldKey` entries inside nested stat-block drafts are now rejected before any `Map` normalization can hide malformed proposals.
  - Sparse or null progression-level entries are now treated as invalid proposals with structured feedback.
  - Progression-level `values` are now guarded before column-presence validation so malformed entries return rejection feedback instead of throwing.



## Dev Notes

### Architecture alignment

- The architecture explicitly says root enforces authority policy and should reject any proposal that changes `createPlan`, introduces `approved`, sets `addressed=true`, mutates the wrong flow or stale revision, or structurally violates the draft surface expected from the plan. [Source: `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture.md` — Mutation policy split / Root enforces authority policy]
- On rejection, root should restore the last legal draft, emit machine-usable feedback, keep the flow alive, and re-send corrected state to the create dialogue child. [Source: `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture.md` — Mutation policy split / Root enforces authority policy]
- Create remains the semantic validator/persister. Root should not take over value-kind/cardinality checks, required-vs-skipped legality, relation endpoint legality, or persistence authority. [Source: `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture.md` — Mutation policy split / Create enforces semantic validity]
- The architecture recommends a single shared mutation-permission module (e.g. `create-draft-mutation-policy.ts`) to avoid drift between root and create. [Source: `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture.md` — Mutation policy split / Single-source mutation policy]

### Previous story intelligence

- Story 1.3 introduced draft revisions and response baselines, which are the root-owned comparison surfaces Story 3.2 should use for stale/illegal proposal checks. [Source: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/1-3-add-draft-revisions-and-response-baselines-for-authority-checks.md`]
- Story 3.1 established root-mediated lookup request/result brokerage; Story 3.2 should build on that flow without changing lookup ownership boundaries. [Source: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/3-1-add-root-mediated-lookup-requests-from-create-dialogue.md`]
- Epic 2 established the response supervisor/create-dialogue child and flow-first routing; Story 3.2 should validate proposals arriving from that child, not re-open ingress or response-structure work. [Source: Epic 2 story artifacts]

### Current code reality to build on

- Root currently captures `WORKFLOW_UPDATE` and applies response drafts into workflow-related state, but there is no current shared create-draft mutation policy enforcement path in root. This gap is already called out by the architecture artifact. [Source: `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture.md` — Current code assessment; `src/stately-studio/chatsendrootmachinev2.ts` search results]
- `WorkflowRecord` already persists authoritative `createPlan`, `createDrafts`, and feedback surfaces, making the root workflow record the right place to compare incoming proposals against the last legal state. [Source: `src/stately-studio/actors/shared/workflow-registry.ts`]
- `entity-creation-engine.ts` is where draft entries currently become `approved` and `addressed=true` through semantic review helpers like `approveEntry()` and `reviewCreateDraftBundle()`. That is strong evidence those semantics belong to create, not root. [Source: `src/stately-studio/actors/entity-creation-engine.ts`]
- The entity creation engine’s feedback generation already produces structured `WorkflowFeedbackItem[]`, which is a useful precedent for machine-usable rejection feedback from root. [Source: `src/stately-studio/actors/entity-creation-engine.ts`]
- There is not yet a shared `create-draft-mutation-policy.ts` or equivalent authority-check module in the brownfield codebase. [Source: current code search results]

### Implementation guidance for the dev agent

- Separate “is this proposal allowed to be attempted?” from “is this proposal semantically valid?”
- Keep root-side checks structural and authority-oriented.
- Reuse the persisted baseline and authoritative draft bundle for comparison; do not trust child-local state as the comparison source.
- Emit structured rejection feedback with stable codes/messages so later dialogue recovery and QA can reason about failure causes.
- If Story 3.3 has not landed yet, make the root-side forwarding seam explicit and typed rather than burying temporary assumptions inline.

### Suggested file touch list

- `src/stately-studio/chatsendrootmachinev2.ts`
- `src/stately-studio/actors/shared/workflow-registry.ts`
- a new shared `create-draft-mutation-policy` module under `src/stately-studio/actors/shared/` or nearby protocol space
- the shared create-dialogue proposal protocol module introduced around Stories 1.3 / 3.1
- `src/stately-studio/createmachine.ts` only insofar as the root → create adjudication seam needs a typed downstream target reference

### Project Structure Notes

- Keep authority-validation work inside `src/stately-studio/` root orchestration, workflow, and shared policy/protocol modules.
- Do not move authority checks into UI/session code, generic server modules, or the create-dialogue child itself.
- Preserve the architecture boundary: root validates authority, create adjudicates semantics, lookup retrieves, response converses.

### Testing Requirements

- Per project-context rules, do not add new tests unless the user explicitly asks for test creation or test updates.
- If the user later approves test updates, keep them narrow and policy-focused:
  - one assertion that proposals trying to set `approved` or `addressed=true` are rejected in root
  - one assertion that stale proposals are rejected using baseline/revision metadata
  - one assertion that structurally legal proposals are forwarded into the create adjudication seam
  - avoid broad end-to-end adjudication tests until Story 3.3 lands
- Prioritize contract verification and architecture alignment over suite growth.

### XState / Stately alignment

- Parent/root should own policy enforcement and downstream handoff decisions.
- Shared policy modules should centralize authority rules rather than duplicating them across actors.
- Create should remain a focused semantic validator/persister actor, not a catch-all router/policy engine.
- Actor contracts should stay explicit and typed for proposal submission, rejection feedback, and adjudication forwarding.

### References
